identity.description: Linear regression of a conditional QUANTILE instead of the mean: minimizes the asymmetric pinball (check) loss, so q=0.5 is median regression and tail q's map the outcome's spread. Makes NO distributional assumption on the errors — the family's distribution-free member, robust to outliers and heteroscedasticity.

consumes.note: continuous target; counts are tolerated but mass points slow IRLS convergence

emits.note: the conditional q-quantile prediction — a distribution-free point, not a mean; closest existing port. portTypeProposal: a 'quantile-band' port for multi-quantile / interval emissions (fitting several q's yields lower/median/upper bands no current port expresses)
per-quantile slopes with kernel-based robust SEs; slopes differing across q IS the heteroscedasticity story

q.note: the quantile to estimate; usually fixed by the use-case (e.g. 0.9 capacity planning) rather than searched

kernel.note: kernel for the robust covariance sandwich

invariances.why: the pinball-loss minimizer is equivariant under affine rescaling of features — coefficients rescale inversely and predictions are identical; no penalty term exists in this driver to break it
the conditional quantile is modeled as LINEAR in x; a monotone transform of an input changes the fit (quantiles ARE equivariant to monotone transforms of the TARGET — a separate, useful property)
the check-loss objective has no missing-value mechanism; rows must be complete
the pinball loss identifies the conditional quantile with NO assumption on the error distribution — no likelihood, no variance law; the family's distribution-free member
the effective information near quantile q comes from the ~min(q,1-q) fraction of local data — tail quantiles (0.05/0.95) need substantially more rows than the median for stable slopes
the linear form extends the conditional quantile beyond the observed covariate range

featureStats.why: under symmetric errors the median and mean lines coincide and OLS is more efficient — quantile regression earns its keep exactly when the conditional distribution is asymmetric or heavy-tailed
spread that varies with x (e.g. Breusch-Pagan on absolute OLS residuals) means quantile slopes genuinely differ across q — the single-mean summary is hiding the story quantiles reveal

heavy ties/discrete mass in y (e.g. many exact zeros) make the check-loss surface piecewise-flat, slowing IRLS and blurring the quantile's identification — a warning toward count/tweedie treatment instead

modelMetrics.why: the proper scoring rule for a quantile forecast — the only honest scoreboard number; MSE would reward reverting to the mean
independently-fitted q's can produce crossing predictions (the 0.9 line below the 0.5 line) — a per-row incoherence rate that flags the multi-quantile emission as needing monotone rearrangement

edgeCases.condition: extreme q with small n (few tail-side points)
edgeCases.behavior: slope estimates dominated by a handful of rows; unstable SEs
quantile crossing — non-monotone predicted quantiles per row
degenerate flat segments in the objective; IRLS convergence warnings
edgeCases.note: raise max_iter; consider a count family instead

driver.constructor: QuantReg(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit(q=..., vcov='robust', kernel='epa', bandwidth='hsheather', max_iter=..., p_tol=...)
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant; one fit per requested q — the wrapper loops q's and stacks predictions for band output
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded IRLS fit; predict is thread-safe; independent q-fits are embarrassingly parallel

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; incomplete rows must be imputed or dropped
the quantile is linear in x; transforming skewed covariates improves that linearity (and target transforms commute with quantiles, a free lunch OLS lacks)
predictions are scale-invariant (no penalty), but standardization makes per-quantile coefficients comparable across features
categoricals must be design-encoded before the objective sees the matrix
